title: Oncall surge mitigation cookbook for dedicated pools
content:
Summary:
This is a compact on-call cookbook we can use for rapid containment of noisy-tenant / pool-degradation events in Dedicated GPU pools. Goal: restore capacity and latency SLOs within 15 minutes, preserve as much client throughput as possible, and capture signals for follow-up. Keep it pragmatic — exact thresholds vary by pool.

Context and recent run:
- Incident observed 2024-11-19 16:12 UTC: p99 latency jump to 3x baseline in pool-gpu-eu-west-1, sustained throughput drop of ~35%.
- Primary symptom: sustained token-throughput drop and increased kernel queue time sampling in nvml. Autoscaler attempted scale-up but then scale-down triggered rapidly, causing thrash.
- Hypothesis at the time: a tenant with runaway KV cache growth and many small, high-concurrency requests was causing queue amplification and eviction storms; autoscale cooldown was too permissive, amplifying oscillation.

Quick priorities for oncall (first 0-15 minutes):
1) Triage and contain (0-5m):
   - Broadcast: post short status in #sre-dedicated-pools. Use template: "Oncall: investigating pool <pool> high-latency, taking containment actions. ETA 15m. INC-xxxx"
   - Identify affected pool(s): prometheus query (replace pool label):
       - p99 latency:  query: latency_request_p99{pool="pool-gpu-eu-west-1"}
       - active requests:  sum(rate(requests_total{pool="pool-gpu-eu-west-1"}[1m])) by (tenant)
   - Quick command: list top tenants by in-flight or tokens:
       - kq: curl -s "${METRICS_URL}/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(inference_tokens_processed_total{pool=\"pool-gpu-eu-west-1\"}[1m])) by (tenant)" | jq .
   - If a tenant accounts for >40% of tokens or in-flight and latency is high, mark them noisy.

2) Immediate containment options (5-12m):
   Option A: Soft-throttle noisy tenant via rate-limit on edge router.
     - Apply temporary rate limit: update envoy route or gateway rule to reduce concurrency to X (start with 50% of baseline). Example snippet (envoy): set "max_requests_per_connection" / route-level per-tenant rate limit.
   Option B: Move noisy tenant to degraded fallback pool (if configured).
     - Use routing policy: route -> fallback-model-small or fallback-region. This keeps requests alive with degraded QOS but frees dedicated capacity.
   Option C: Evict selected tenant from pool (hard containment).
     - kubectl exec into pool-allocator, run: python tools/evict_tenant.py --pool pool-gpu-eu-west-1 --tenant TENANT_ID --reason "noisy-tenant-containment"
     - Note: eviction will drop active requests for that tenant. Use only if throttling/fallbacks fail.

3) Stabilize autoscaler (6-15m):
   - If autoscaler oscillation observed, pause autoscale or extend cooldown:
       - PATCH autoscaler config: set scaleDownCooldownSeconds: 600 (temporary) and scaleUpAggression: conservative.
       - Command (kubectl patch or via console): kubectl patch hpa dedicated-pool-<id> --type merge -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":600}}}}'
   - If control-plane UI available, flip autoscale to manual and add nodes if necessary to quickly restore headroom.

4) Short-term observer actions (0-15m):
   - Capture traces and profiles from a few representative requests for the noisy tenant (trace ids).
   - Grab nvml/nvidia-smi snapshot from affected hosts: for host in $HOSTS; do ssh $host "nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv" > /tmp/nvmi-$host; done
   - Prometheus queries to save to incident page:
       - GPU util variance:  query: stddev_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization{pool="pool-gpu-eu-west-1"}[5m])
       - GPU kernel queue time proxy: query: avg_over_time(kernel_queue_ms{pool="pool-gpu-eu-west-1"}[1m])
       - KV cache growth: query: sum(kv_cache_entries{tenant!=""}) by (tenant)

Evidence collection checklist (do this while containing):
- Save top-10 tenants by token rate (CSV).
- Save top GPU host nvml snapshots.
- Export autoscaler event log for the period +/- 30m.
- Note exact timestamps for any manual evictions or throttle rules.

Investigation notes and heuristics learned (notes-to-self style):
- Noisy tenants often show: many short requests (~<300 tokens) at high QPS, large number of context loads, inefficient batching patterns in the client, or accidental feedback loops (client retries on partial timeouts).
- Signs of KV cache amplification: rising kv_cache_entries + p50/p95 KV lookup latency + drop in batching efficiency (batch_size histogram shifts to 1/2).
- Autoscaler misconfig: default scaleDownCooldownSeconds sometimes too low (e.g., 60s) — with noisy evictions this causes rapid scale-down that starves remaining tenants.

Runbook: step-by-step (condensed)
- Step 0: Confirm pool-level SLO breaches (latency p99 > 2x target OR throughput drop >20%).
- Step 1: Identify top contributing tenant(s) with token-based rank.
- Step 2: Try applying soft throttle (edge/gateway) for 5m.
- Step 3: If throttle insufficient, move tenant to fallback routing.
- Step 4: If still insufficient AND quota violations persist, evict tenant from pool (record impact).
- Step 5: Stabilize autoscaler (increase cooldown / pause).
- Step 6: Monitor for 30m stability then start controlled rollback of throttles/evictions back to normal with gradational steps.

Escalation criteria and owners:
- If containment fails within 15 minutes: escalate to SRE lead (oncall pager) and owner for Dedicated infra (Aisha Khan).
- If eviction required and more than 3 tenants affected: declare major incident and page eng-lead.

Examples of useful PromQL (copyable):
- Top tenants by token rate in 1m: topk(10, sum(rate(inference_tokens_processed_total{pool="pool-gpu-eu-west-1"}[1m])) by (tenant))
- Autoscaler activity: kube_hpa_status_current_replicas{hpa="dedicated-pool-gpu-eu-west-1"}
- Eviction events: events_total{reason=~"Evict.*"} | grep pool-gpu-eu-west-1 (or equivalent)

Post-incident follow-ups (owner + target date):
- Aisha: increase default scaleDownCooldownSeconds to 300 for pools in region eu-west-1 (target: 2024-12-15).
- Marco: add a routing primitive to perform automated soft-throttling based on tenant token-share >40% (prototype by 2025-01-10).
- Priya (me): add a small dashboard panel that shows tenant token-share percentile and kv_cache_entries for quick triage (complete: 2024-12-01).
- SRE: run a synthetic load test that mimics many small requests to validate autoscaler > 2024-12-05.

Longer term mitigations and product asks:
- Implement a tenant-level fairness enforcer in allocator that can apply gradual backpressure before eviction.
- Add adaptive autoscale heuristics aware of eviction events and kv-cache-growth signals.
- Product: provide an SDK guidance note to customers about batching hints to avoid micro-QPS patterns.

Incident artifact snippets (copy to incident doc):
- Eviction command used: python tools/evict_tenant.py --pool pool-gpu-eu-west-1 --tenant t-8934 --reason "noisy-tenant-containment-20241119" --force
- Autoscaler patch we applied: kubectl patch hpa dedicated-pool-gpu-eu-west-1 --type merge -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":600}}}}'

Things to watch for in follow-up review:
- Did throttling increase client error rates (4xx/5xx) for the tenant? Capture error budget impact.
- Was there a config drift that allowed a newly onboarded tenant to overwhelm cache limits?
- Check canary behavior when rollback throttles: ensure no surge flapping.

Notes / loose ideas (brainstorm):
- Could we auto-detect "batch starvation" by watching batch_size_histogram moving to 1 and tie that to an auto-throttle?
- Consider a short-lived quota token-pool per tenant with borrowable credits that decay (prevents sudden bursts).

Appendix: useful quick commands and locations
- Get list of active tenants in pool: curl -s "$ROUTER/api/pools/pool-gpu-eu-west-1/tenants" | jq .
- Grab autoscaler events: kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler -n infra --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | grep dedicated-pool-gpu-eu-west-1
- NVML snapshots: for host in $(cat hosts-list.txt); do ssh $host "nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory,utilization.gpu --format=csv"; done

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Formalize throttle play into platform console (Marco).
- [ ] Add Kv-cache per-tenant metric to default pool dashboard (Priya).
- [ ] Run chaos-test that simulates many tiny requests from single tenant and measure autoscaler reactions (SRE team).

Last oncall anecdote (keep):
We tried soft-throttle first and saw steady improvement. After we extended the autoscale cooldown the pool stopped oscillating and p99 returned to baseline in ~18 minutes. Manual eviction was not needed, but we recorded the eviction command for the runbook because some customers will require it.

If you update this doc: add timestamped notes at top and keep a short one-line summary of actions taken during future incidents.

-- Priya
